title: Black, White and Read All Over

bands.1:
At three o'clock, the crew creeps through the old lava tube.

Krak is not with you. "I will meet you inside," he said. He did not say how.

"What's black and white and read all over?" whispers Mo. "A newspaper!"

The tunnel ends at a gold grate. Beyond it is the Edit Bay. Editors in gold tracksuits snore at their desks. A sign says, "RULE ONE: IF MAXX LOOKS BAD, CUT IT."

Creatures sit in cages. Scorchquill is locked in a glass box.

Then the biggest editor sits up. He takes off his gold cap.

It is Krak!

"I got a job here last week," he whispers. "Night editor. Strike that. The worst night editor they have ever had."

He opens a drawer. "The password is FLAWLESSME. I watched Maxx type it."

Inside is a gold hard drive. It says, "RAW FOOTAGE. NEVER SHOW ANYONE. (I LOOK SWEATY.)"

On the screen, Maxx is on his gold jet ski. He throws a net over a tiny Creature with his own hands.

"Now I rescue it," Maxx says. "Pass the onions."

You take the drive. That's the proof. Wren and Krak open the cages.

"The Reef Rays scored!" squeaks Tully.

The editors wake up. Goldies run in.

Gus opens a jar of rotten eggs. It stinks like volcano gas.

"The volcano is going to blow!" yells a Goldie. They all run.

One Goldie blocks the door. His card says, "Do NOT let them leave."

You hand the card to Scorchquill. You point at NOT.

Scorchquill burns a line through it.

"Do let them leave," reads the Goldie. He holds the door open.

"They cut my NOT," says Krak. "We cut theirs."

Back at Krak's office, you play the last clip. Maxx is on a big yacht.

"The finale is LIVE," he says. "No edits. It has to go perfectly."

"No edits," says Krak. "So if it goes wrong, the whole world sees."
bands.2:
At three o'clock in the morning, the crew creeps into the old lava tube. It is pitch black and hot enough to bake bread.

Chief Editor Krak is not with you. He gave you his badge, drew the route in red pen and said, "I will meet you inside." He did not say how.

Indi's disguises are copies of the Redpen Rumble with eyeholes cut in the front page. Mo's newspaper is upside down.

"What's black and white and read all over?" whispers Mo. "A newspaper!"

Everyone groans.

The tunnel ends at a gold grate. Beyond it is the Edit Bay, a red-lit room full of screens. Editors in gold tracksuits snore at their desks. A sign says, "RULE ONE: IF MAXX LOOKS BAD, CUT IT."

Along the back wall are cages. In a fireproof box marked "AUTO-EDITOR (TEST)" sits Scorchquill, her crest glowing dimly.

Then the biggest editor of all sits up and takes off his gold cap. Underneath is a green visor, and eyebrows like burnt toast.

"Krak!" squeaks Indi.

"Night editor, since last Tuesday," says Krak. "Strike that. Worst night editor in the building. I have cut nothing all week."

"Why didn't you tell us?" whispers Zed.

"An editor checks a story before he prints it."

He opens a drawer in his desk. "Password's FLAWLESSME. I watched him type it."

Inside is a gold hard drive: "RAW FOOTAGE. NEVER SHOW ANYONE. (I LOOK SWEATY.)"

On the big screen, Maxx sits on his gold jet ski. He throws a gold net over a tiny Creature with his own hands. "Okay. Now I rescue it. Somebody pass the onions."

You pocket the drive. That's the proof. Wren and Krak open the cages.

Then Tully's radio crackles. "The Reef Rays scored a goal!" she squeaks, too loudly.

Every editor wakes up. Goldies pour in.

Gus opens a jar of rotten eggs. "Volcano gas!" yells a Goldie. "She's going to blow!" Everyone runs.

Only one Goldie stays, blocking the door. He reads from a card: "Do NOT let them leave."

You take the card and hold it up to Scorchquill, one finger on the word NOT. She burns a neat black line through it.

"Do let them leave," reads the Goldie. He shrugs and holds the door open.

"They cut my NOT," says Krak. "We cut theirs."

Back at the Rumble office, you play the last clip on the drive. Maxx is on a huge yacht at night.

"The big finale is LIVE," he says. "No cuts. No edits. So it has to go perfectly."

"Live," says Krak slowly. "Then if anything goes wrong, the whole world sees it."
bands.3:
At three o'clock in the morning, the crew creeps into the old lava tube. It is pitch black and hot enough to bake bread, and Snipwing bats flit overhead, listening to their own echoes.

Chief Editor Krak is not with you. He gave you his badge, drew the route in red pen across the crater map and said only, "I will meet you inside." He did not say how.

Indi's disguises are copies of the Redpen Rumble with eyeholes cut through the front page. Mo's is upside down.

"What's black and white and read all over?" whispers Mo. "A newspaper!"

Everyone groans.

Gus pats a jar sealed with three layers of tape. "The Eggsplosion," he whispers. "Twelve eggs rotting under my bunk since Easter. Volcano gas smells like rotten eggs."

The tunnel ends at a gold grate. Beyond it lies the Edit Bay, a long red-lit room with a wall of glowing screens. Editors in gold tracksuits are snoring at their desks. A sign above them reads, "RULE ONE: IF MAXX LOOKS BAD, CUT IT."

Along the back wall are cages: Nodrakes, Barkindles and a Whetwing with its wings pinned. In a fireproof glass box marked "AUTO-EDITOR (TEST)" sits Scorchquill, her crest feathers glowing dim and sad.

Then the biggest editor in the room stops snoring, sits up and takes off his gold cap. Underneath is a green visor, a red pen the size of a carrot, and a pair of eyebrows like burnt toast.

"Krak!" squeaks Indi, much too loudly. Nobody else wakes.

"Night editor, since last Tuesday," Krak whispers. "Strike that. Worst night editor in the building. I haven't cut a single second all week."

"Why didn't you tell us?" whispers Zed.

"An editor checks every fact before he prints the story," says Krak. "You were the last fact."

He slides open a drawer in his desk. "Password's FLAWLESSME. I watched him type it on Thursday."

Inside is a gold hard drive: "RAW FOOTAGE. NEVER SHOW ANYONE. (I LOOK SWEATY.)"

On the big screen, Maxx sits on his gold jet ski, red-faced and sweating. A tiny Creature paddles in front of him, and Maxx throws a gold net over it with his own hands. "Ugh, it's looking at me. Throw it again," he snaps. Then he grins at the camera. "Okay. Now I rescue it. Somebody pass the onions."

You pocket the drive. That's the proof. Wren and Krak open the cages, and Scorchquill leaps onto Krak's shoulder, crest blazing red again.

Then Tully's footy radio crackles. "The Reef Rays scored a goal!" she squeaks, far too loudly.

Every editor sits bolt upright. Alarms wail, and Goldies pour through the doors.

Gus rips the tape off the Eggsplosion. "Volcano gas!" yells a Goldie. "She's going to blow!" Editors and Goldies stampede for the exit.

Only one Goldie stays, blocking the door. He reads slowly from a card: "Orders from Maxx. Do NOT let them leave."

You pluck the card from his fingers and hold it up to Scorchquill, one finger on the word NOT. She breathes on it, and a neat black line burns straight through.

"Do let them leave," the Goldie reads. He frowns, shrugs and holds the door open. "Orders are orders."

"They cut my NOT," says Krak. "So we cut theirs."

Back at the Rumble office, you play the last clip on the drive. Maxx is on the deck of a huge yacht at night.

"Note for the big finale," he says. "It's LIVE. No cuts. No edits. So when I catch THE BIG ONE, it has to go perfectly."

Krak's eyebrows rise like smoke. "Live," he says. "Then if anything goes wrong, the whole world sees it."
bands.4:
At three o'clock in the morning, the crew creeps into the old lava tube, which is pitch black, hot enough to bake bread and full of Snipwing bats flitting overhead, listening to their own echoes.

Chief Editor Krak is not with you. He pinned his badge to your jacket, drew the route across the crater map in red pen and said only, "I will meet you inside." When Zed asked how, Krak crossed the question out.

Indi's disguise of the Chapter is a copy of the Redpen Rumble each, with eyeholes cut through the front page. "Nobody looks twice at someone reading the paper," she says. Mo's is upside down.

"What's black and white and read all over?" whispers Mo.

Everyone groans before he can finish, including a Snipwing.

"And then we go left," whispers Zed, "and then we go right, and then..." A Snipwing swoops past his ear with a sharp snip, and Zed, quite suddenly, stops saying "and then".

Gus pats a jar sealed with three layers of tape: twelve eggs that have been rotting under his bunk since Easter. Volcano gas, he reminds everyone, smells exactly like rotten eggs.

The tunnel ends at a gold grate. Beyond it lies the Edit Bay, a long room lit red by a wall of screens, where editors in gold tracksuits snore at their desks with their headphones on. Above them hangs a sign: "RULE ONE: IF MAXX LOOKS BAD, CUT IT."

Along the back wall are cages: Nodrakes, Barkindles, a Whetwing with its wings pinned and a Strandle plucking at the bars. In a fireproof glass box marked "AUTO-EDITOR (TEST)" sits Scorchquill, her crest feathers glowing the colour of a dying barbecue.

Then the largest of the snoring editors stops snoring. He sits up, stretches, and removes his gold cap, and beneath it are a green visor, a red pen the size of a carrot and a pair of eyebrows like burnt toast.

"Krak!" squeaks Indi. Nobody else so much as twitches.

"Night editor, since last Tuesday," Krak whispers. "Strike that. Worst night editor in the building. In a whole week, I haven't cut a single second."

"Why didn't you tell us?" hisses Zed.

"An editor checks every fact before he prints the story." He looks at the crew, one at a time, as if proofreading you. "You were the last fact."

He slides open a drawer in his own desk. "Password's FLAWLESSME. He types it with one finger, and very slowly."

Inside lies a gold hard drive: "RAW FOOTAGE. NEVER SHOW ANYONE. (I LOOK SWEATY.)"

On the big screen, Maxx sits on his gold jet ski, red-faced and sweating, while a tiny Creature paddles in the sea in front of him. He throws a gold net over it with his own hands. The net, if you look closely, has his logo on it. "Ugh, it's looking at me. Throw it again," he snaps, and then, to the camera, with the famous grin: "Okay. Now I rescue it. Somebody pass the onions."

Indi says nothing. She has seen this rescue before, on the day you set sail, with music, and tears, and none of this.

You pocket the drive while Wren and Krak work along the cages. Scorchquill leaps onto Krak's shoulder, and her crest, for the first time in weeks, blazes red to the tips.

Then the footy radio in Tully's pocket crackles. "The Reef Rays scored a goal!" she squeaks, a great deal too loudly.

Every editor sits bolt upright. Alarms wail, and Goldies pour through the doors.

Gus rips the tape off the Eggsplosion. A grey-green stink rolls across the room, and somebody yells, "Volcano gas! She's going to blow!" Editors and Goldies stampede for the exit with their noses pinched.

Only one Goldie stays, planted in the doorway, reading aloud from a card with the care of someone who does not read often: "Orders from Maxx. Do NOT let them leave."

You pluck the card from his fingers and hold it up to Scorchquill, one finger resting on a single word. She breathes on it, gently, and a neat black line burns straight through the NOT.

"Do let them leave," the Goldie reads. He frowns, shrugs and steps aside. "Orders are orders."

"They cut my NOT," says Krak, with enormous satisfaction. "So we cut theirs."

Outside, the Creatures scatter across the warm black rock, and the Whetwing shoots up into the smoke like a rocket.

Back in the crooked office of the Redpen Rumble, you play the last clip on the drive. It is night, on the deck of a huge yacht, and Maxx is talking to his editors.

"Note for the big finale," he says. "It's LIVE. No cuts. No edits. So when I catch THE BIG ONE, it has to go perfectly."

Krak leans back, very slowly, and his eyebrows rise like smoke from the crater.

"Live," he says. "No edits." He uncaps the giant red pen, and for once he does not cross anything out. "Then if anything goes wrong, the whole world sees it."
